findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages instead of 1, and for 100/50 it yields 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, and the next action advances offset to user_count, causing findMembers to render an empty extra page.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset values
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from request parameters with only to_i conversion. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an entire large group in one request, or supply negative values that can produce database errors. The server should clamp limit to a sane maximum and clamp both values to be non-negative instead of trusting the JavaScript client to do so.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates groups to the first 50 members
findings.body: The members endpoint now always applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. The public group-members route/template has no pagination controls or next/previous actions (those exist only in the admin controller), so for any group with more than 50 members the remaining members become unreachable in the public UI.

findings.title: Group creation ignores the alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The JavaScript asJSON payload includes alias_level and the admin form exposes the alias-level selector before saving, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A newly created group therefore silently gets the database default alias_level (0/nobody) regardless of what the admin selected, while update does honor alias_level, making create and update inconsistent.

findings.title: Remove-member control is shown for automatic groups
findings.body: The template guards the remove link with {{#unless automatic}}, but this item view's context is the individual member (a User), not the group, so automatic is undefined/falsy and the remove control renders even for automatic groups. Clicking it calls the admin endpoint which rejects automatic-group changes with 422, and the model's removeMember/addMembers promises have no error handler, so the failure is silent to the admin.

findings.title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group name is empty
findings.body: findMembers previously returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) for an empty name, preserving its promise contract; it now bare-returns undefined. Any caller that chains .then() on the result (the pattern the old routes used) will throw a TypeError for unsaved/nameless groups. It should return a resolved promise to keep the contract uniform with the AJAX path.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb only maps DELETE to remove_member. Because controller specs bypass routing, the test passes even though it never exercises the real request path; it should use :delete like the successful-removal example below it, so a routing/verb regression would be caught.

findings.title: add_members crashes if usernames is supplied as an array parameter
findings.body: add_members calls usernames.split(',') assuming params[:usernames] is always a String. A request sending usernames as an array (e.g. usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b, a natural form-encoded API input) makes params[:usernames] an Array and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of adding members or a clean 4xx. The action should normalize Array and String inputs before splitting.
